threshold_basis: pooled median across the reference seasons, fixed so a score means the same thing in every season

Outside hitter.label: Hitting efficiency, adjusted for passing load

setter_attack_bonus.note: awarded on kills per set, not hitting efficiency: production repeats (split-half .82) where efficiency on ~20 season attempts does not (.25)

outside_passing_adjustment.note: fitted with attack volume controlled; pooling without it gives -0.0003 and adjusts nothing, because high-volume attackers both pass more and hit better

opponent_adjustment.model: rate(player i vs team j) = mu + player_i - opponent_j, per season
opponent_adjustment.fit: alternating weighted means, weighted by the denominator; ridge 25 on opponent effects only
opponent_adjustment.applies_to: the rating only; benchmarks_met stays raw so the badge remains readable
opponent_adjustment.rejected_alternative: regressing on season schedule strength. Mean opponent offence and defence correlate 0.993 so the fit is unidentified, and deep teams play hard schedules, so it reads roster depth as opponent difficulty. It moved Texas's 2025 outside from 4.69 kills per set down to 4.47 and Jackson State's up from 4.03 to 4.20.
opponent_adjustment.does_not_fix: usage. An outside taking 40% of a thin team's swings out-produces one of four good attackers per set, and that is not the opponent's doing.

recency_rule.rule: at least one set played in the team's last three matches
recency_rule.note: applied to the season still being played, so a season total frozen by injury stops holding a ranking it is no longer being tested for. Finished seasons rank everyone who met the set minimum.

rank_band.method: each player's matches split odd/even and scored twice; the standard deviation of the half-to-half difference, halved for the full sample and pooled by sets played, is the standard error
rank_band.interval: 90% (1.645 standard errors either side of the rating)
rank_band.note: a rank out of a thousand looks precise and is not. Publish the band, not the rank, whenever the band is wide.
